papers.name: Paper 1 Computational thinking and programming skills

topics.name: 3.1 Fundamentals of algorithms
points: 3.1.1 Representing algorithms: what an algorithm is; decomposition and abstraction
3.1.1 Representing algorithms using pseudo-code, program code and flowcharts; inputs, processing and outputs
3.1.1 Determining the purpose of simple algorithms using trace tables and visual inspection
3.1.2 Efficiency of algorithms (time efficiency)
3.1.3 Searching algorithms: linear search and binary search, compared
3.1.4 Sorting algorithms: merge sort and bubble sort, compared

topics.name: 3.2 Programming
points: 3.2.1 Data types: integer, real, Boolean, character and string
3.2.2 Programming concepts: variables, constants, assignment, iteration, selection and subroutines
3.2.2 Definite and indefinite iteration; nested selection and iteration; meaningful identifier names
3.2.3 Arithmetic operations, including integer division and remainder
3.2.4 Relational operations
3.2.5 Boolean operations: NOT, AND and OR
3.2.6 Data structures: one- and two-dimensional arrays and records
3.2.7 Input/output
3.2.8 String handling operations and conversions between strings, integers and reals
3.2.9 Random number generation
3.2.10 Structured programming and subroutines: parameters, return values, local variables, advantages of the structured approach
3.2.11 Robust and secure programming: data validation and simple authentication routines
3.2.11 Testing: normal, boundary and erroneous test data; syntax and logic errors

topics.name: 3.3 Fundamentals of data representation
points: 3.3.1 Number bases: decimal, binary and hexadecimal; why hexadecimal is used
3.3.2 Converting between number bases (0 to 255)
3.3.3 Units of information: bits, bytes and decimal prefixes kilo to tera
3.3.4 Binary arithmetic: adding binary numbers and logical binary shifts
3.3.5 Character encoding: ASCII and Unicode
3.3.6 Representing images: pixels, resolution, colour depth and bitmap file size
3.3.7 Representing sound: sampling rate, sample resolution and sound file size
3.3.8 Data compression: Huffman coding
3.3.8 Data compression: run length encoding (RLE)

topics.name: 3.4 Computer systems
points: 3.4.1 Hardware and software
3.4.2 Boolean logic: truth tables for NOT, AND, OR and XOR
3.4.2 Boolean logic: logic circuit diagrams and Boolean expressions
3.4.3 Software classification: system and application software; operating systems and utility programs
3.4.4 Classification of programming languages: high-level and low-level, machine code and assembly language
3.4.4 Translators: interpreters, compilers and assemblers
3.4.5 Systems architecture: CPU components (ALU, control unit, clock, registers, buses) and main memory
3.4.5 CPU performance: clock speed, number of cores and cache size; the Fetch-Execute cycle
3.4.5 Memory: RAM, ROM, cache and registers; volatile and non-volatile
3.4.5 Secondary storage: solid state and magnetic storage; cloud storage
3.4.5 Embedded and non-embedded systems

topics.name: 3.5 Fundamentals of computer networks
points: What a computer network is; advantages and disadvantages of networks
Network types: PAN, LAN and WAN
Wired and wireless networks; cable types; advantages and disadvantages of wireless
Network protocols: TCP, IP, HTTP, HTTPS, SMTP and IMAP
Network security: authentication, encryption, firewalls and MAC address filtering
The 4-layer TCP/IP model and the layers at which protocols operate

topics.name: 3.6 Cyber security
points: 3.6.1 Fundamentals of cyber security
3.6.2 Cyber security threats: pharming, weak passwords, misconfigured access rights, removable media, unpatched software
3.6.2 Penetration testing: insider and external
3.6.2.1 Social engineering: blagging, phishing and shouldering
3.6.2.2 Malicious code (malware): viruses, trojans and spyware
3.6.3 Methods to detect and prevent threats: biometrics, passwords, CAPTCHA, email confirmations, automatic software updates

topics.name: 3.7 Relational databases and structured query language (SQL)
points: 3.7.1 Relational databases: tables, records, fields, data types, primary and foreign keys
3.7.1 How relational databases reduce data inconsistency and redundancy
3.7.2 SQL: retrieving data with SELECT, FROM, WHERE and ORDER BY (up to two tables)
3.7.2 SQL: INSERT INTO, UPDATE and DELETE

topics.name: 3.8 Ethical, legal and environmental impacts of digital technology on wider society, including issues of privacy
points: Ethical, legal and environmental impacts and risks of digital technology on society
Data privacy issues: citizens' privacy versus government and security services' access
Contexts: cyber security, mobile technologies, wireless networking and cloud storage
Contexts: hacking, wearable technologies, computer-based implants and autonomous vehicles
